text:
Korean stocks opened more than 2 percent lower Monday as investors dumped major technology shares, tracking Wall Street losses amid concerns over the artificial intelligence (AI) sector.
After opening 2.77 percent lower, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell 129.7 points, or 2.66 percent, to 4,740.26 as of 9:15 a.m.
On Friday, the KOSPI plunged 5.21 percent, falling below the psychologically important 5,000 mark and marking the lowest closing level in about 10 months since Jan. 16, when it finished at 4,840.74.
On Friday (local time), U.S. stocks also tumbled, putting Wall Street on track for its longest losing streak since 2020.
Investor sentiment was dampened by growing concerns over tighter U.S. semiconductor export restrictions, following reports that Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD), like Nvidia Corp., could face risks related to its business with China.
The concerns weighed on markets despite a successful initial public offering by AI startup Anthropic.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.93 percent, while the S&P 500 dropped 3.7 percent and the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite slid 5.28 percent.
Market bellwether Samsung Electronics fell 3.39 percent, while its chipmaking rival SK hynix declined 2.34 percent.
Top carmaker Hyundai Motor dropped 3.73 percent, and pharmaceutical giant Samsung Biologics fell 4.21 percent.
The Korean won was quoted at 1,338.8 won against the U.S. dollar as of 9:15 a.m., up 7.2 won from the previous trading session's close.
